8	/-!
9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
15	
16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
23	
24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
25	
26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
32	
33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
34	
35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
40	  the freedom.
41	
42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
57	  chart parameter.
58	-/
59	
60	set_option autoImplicit false
61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
62	
63	universe u
64	
65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
66	
67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
71	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
72	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
73	
74	noncomputable section
75	
76	variable (C π) in
77	/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**
78	
79	Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
80	`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
81	*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
82	requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.
83	
84	The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
85	that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
86	def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
89	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
90	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
91	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
92	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
93	    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
94	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
95	
96	variable (C π) in
97	/-- **Heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate**: the `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter
98	family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.
99	
100	So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
101	different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
102	condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
104	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
105	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
106	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
108	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
109	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
110	    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
111	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
112	  huniv i
113	
114	variable (C π) in
115	/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**
116	
117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
118	question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
119	never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
120	carries no uniformity obligation.
121	
122	Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
123	CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
124	than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
125	def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
126	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
127	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
128	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
129	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
130	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
131	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
132	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
133	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
134	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
135	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
136	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
137	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
138	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf
139	
140	end
141	
142	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# COVERAGE NEEDS NO DROP, NO ORACLE, AND NO STEP 6
11	
12	A retraction of this lane's own account of B-5, and it removes a residue rather than adding one.
13	
14	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageTest.lean`'s DEFECT section establishes — correctly — that the
15	`w4-datb` §1.2 argument as written runs the greedy drop at `Z := 0` and feeds the drop's
16	**output** `Σ` back as the chart index's `Z`, so that the two stages carry different `Z`, and
17	that this feedback ("step 6") is not discharged anywhere.  It records step 6 as one of B-5's
18	open residues.
19	
20	**Step 6 is not a residue, because coverage does not need the drop at all.**
21	
22	## Why: read what `chartLocus` actually asks for
23	
24	`IsSplitWitness` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:151`) — and its own docstring says this at length, under
25	"A convention this predicate INHERITS" — asks for a divisor `W` in the presenting class with
26	`Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))`, and asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  Effectivity and the
27	degree normalisation are what the *chart map's injectivity* needs (GAP-2, `h⁰ = 1`), not what
28	*membership of the locus* needs.
29	
30	The drop (`RiemannRoch/CoverageDrop.lean`) exists to manufacture exactly those two extra
31	properties: it takes a degree-`g+e` witness with `h¹ = 0` and produces an effective `S` with
32	`h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1`.  For membership, that work is thrown away — `mem_chartLocus_of_drop` returns
33	the `IsSplitWitness` half from `hW₀`/`h1` alone, and its own proof shows this: the split witness
34	comes from `isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ m Z M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ h1`, in which the drop,
35	the oracle `P`, `hdense`, `hPcl`, `hPdeg`, `g`, `e`, `hχ` and `hdeg` **do not appear**.
36	
37	So the feedback of step 6 was an artefact of routing coverage through the drop.  Cut the drop
38	and there is one `Z` again — the chart index's — and nothing to feed back.
39	
40	## What coverage then needs, in full
41	
42	Exactly one input beyond the landed splitting: a divisor of the twisted fibre class over the
43	splitting field with vanishing `H¹`.  That is DAT-0a at the fibre field, and it is genuinely
44	per-fibre (I-0204, `w4-datb` §0.2.2): no uniform `m₀` exists, so the exponent `m` must be chosen
45	against `L`'s own threshold `b_L`.
46	
47	**RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (I-0660).**  This paragraph continued: `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound`
48	"takes `b_L` in exactly the shape `exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`
49	produces it, and *derives* the `m` — so what remains of step 3 is instantiating DAT-0a at the
50	base-changed curve, not choosing anything."  That is FALSE.  At a chart index legal at parameter
51	`n` the `hdeg` hypothesis **forces `b = n`**, and at `n = g` the resulting `hb` is a statement
52	that is false in general — see the retraction note on
53	`mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` itself and `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` for the
54	three machine-checked statements that replace it.  The theorem below is sound; only this account
55	of what remains was wrong.
56	
57	## Main declarations
58	
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1` — **coverage, drop-free**: a splitting plus a
60	  vanishing witness in the twisted class gives `t ∈ chartLocus`.  No `g`, no `e`, no `χ`, no
61	  oracle, no effectivity.
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` — the same with the witness *produced*
63	  from a degree threshold at the splitting field.  Sound; but read its retraction note before
64	  reading the threshold as DAT-0a's (it is forced to equal the chart parameter, I-0660).
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` — the `∃ m` form: the coverage
66	  statement `w4-datb` §1.2 targets, at a fixed chart-index shape.
67	-/

92	/-! ## Coverage without the drop -/
93	
94	variable (C) in
95	/-- **COVERAGE, DROP-FREE** — `w4-datb` §1.2 with steps 4, 5 and 6 deleted rather than
96	discharged.
97	
98	For a point `t` of an arbitrary test `T` and a plus class `lam`: given a finite separable
99	`L/κ(t)` presenting the fibre class by `M₀`, and **any** divisor `W` of the twisted class over
100	`L` with `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))`, the point `t` lies in `chartLocus C m Z lam`.
101	
102	Compare `mem_chartLocus_of_drop`, whose membership half this strictly generalises: that theorem
103	additionally takes `g`, `e`, `hχ`, `hdeg` and a four-part point oracle, and uses none of them
104	for the membership conclusion.  Dropping them is what removes step 6's feedback — the drop's
105	output `Σ` was the only reason two different `Z`s were in play. -/
106	theorem mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1 {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
107	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
108	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L]
109	    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L]
110	    [Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L]
111	    [Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L]
112	    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
113	    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L
114	        (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t) (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam))
115	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
116	    (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
117	    (hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W
118	      = M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
119	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)) :
120	    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
121	  mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre C m Z lam t
122	    (isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam) m Z M₀ hM₀
123	      W hW h1)

125	/-! ## Producing the witness from a degree threshold -/
126	
127	variable (C) in
128	/-- **Coverage from a vanishing threshold at the splitting field.**  The theorem is TRUE and
129	correctly proved; the paragraph that described `hb` as "DAT-0a's threshold, so the twist exponent
130	is *derived*" was WRONG and is retracted below.
131	
132	`hb`: every divisor of degree `≥ b` on `C_L` has vanishing `H¹`.  `hdeg`: the twisted presenting
133	class has `classDeg = b`, which `classDeg_presenting_twist`
134	(`Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean`) computes as `m·d₁ − deg_k Z` for a degree-zero `lam`.
135	Every divisor of the class has that degree (`classDeg_picClass`), so the threshold applies to the
136	representative `exists_picClass_eq` produces, and `mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1` finishes.  No
137	effectivity is needed anywhere, which is why no drop appears.
138	
139	**RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (I-0660; adjudicated in `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean`).**  The
140	claim that `hdeg` is "*supplied*, not assumed, once the chart index is fixed", i.e. that `b` may
141	be taken to be DAT-0a's bound, is FALSE at the parameter that matters:
142	
143	* at a chart index legal at parameter `n` (`deg_k Z = m·d₁ − n`, which
144	  `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup` requires) `hdeg` **forces `b = n`** — it determines `b` rather
145	  than accepting it (`ledger_forces_b_eq_n`);
146	* at `n = g`, `hb` at `b = g` forces **every** degree-`g` divisor to have `h⁰ = 1`
147	  (`hb_forces_h0_eq_one`), which is false on a curve with a moving degree-`g` family.  DAT-0a's
148	  own bound is `n₁·deg F + g` with `0 < deg F`, i.e. strictly above `g` for `n₁ ≥ 1`.
149	
150	What survives: `hdeg` is not unsatisfiable — for any `b ≥ 0` a legal index at parameter `b.toNat`
151	satisfies it by construction (`index_of_threshold`), since `n` is free throughout the chart layer.
152	So this theorem is usable, and the residue of B-5 step 3 is the reconciliation of the chart
153	parameter with the threshold, not an instantiation of DAT-0a. -/
154	theorem mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T)
155	    (t : T.left) (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
156	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L]
157	    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L]
158	    [Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L]
159	    [Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L]
160	    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
161	    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L
162	        (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t) (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam))
163	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
164	    -- The `classDeg L` of `hdeg` is applied to a `relCurve`-spelled class, and the
165	    -- `BaseChangeInstances` pack is keyed to the PRODUCT spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`,
166	    -- so these three do not synthesise in the STATEMENT (a `haveI` in the proof is too late).
167	    -- They are not new assumptions: `instIsIntegralBaseChange`,
168	    -- `instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange` and `instQuasiCompactBaseChange` discharge
169	    -- them at every instantiation, and the proof below re-derives the rest of the pack.
170	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
171	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
172	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
173	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
174	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
175	    (b : ℤ)
176	    (hb : ∀ D : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
177	      b ≤ Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D →
178	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L D) 1))
179	    (hdeg : classDeg L (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
180	      (chartTwistClass C m Z)) = b) :
181	    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam := by
182	  -- The instance pack of `BaseChangeInstances` is keyed to the PRODUCT spelling
183	  -- `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`, not to the `relCurve` alias, so the `relCurve`-spelled
184	  -- binders of `exists_picClass_eq` / `classDeg_picClass` do not synthesise without these
185	  -- re-keyings (the same pack `Pic0ChartCoverageFibre.lean:130` needs).  The `hdeg`/`M₀`
186	  -- binders are therefore stated in the PRODUCT spelling, so that the statement itself needs
187	  -- no re-keying — `relCurveMap C k L` is `(C ◁ overSpecMap (ofId k L)).left`
188	  -- (`relCurveMap_eq_overSpecMap_ofId`), which is also the spelling
189	  -- `classDeg_presenting_twist` delivers.
190	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
191	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
192	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
193	  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
194	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
195	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
196	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
197	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
198	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
199	  obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := Scheme.CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq L
200	    (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
201	  refine mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1 C lam t m Z M₀ hM₀ W hW (hb W ?_)
202	  rw [show Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W
203	      = classDeg L (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W) from (classDeg_picClass L W).symm,
204	    hW, hdeg]
205	
206	variable (C) in
207	/-- **The coverage statement in `∃`-form**, i.e. `w4-datb` §1.2's target shape at a fixed chart
208	index: at a point whose splitting is known and whose twisted class hits the threshold, there is
209	a chart the point belongs to.
210	
211	Trivial given the previous theorem; recorded because it is the shape the DAT-B B-6 packaging
212	(`IsLocallySurjective`) consumes, and because keeping it separate makes visible that the only
213	`∃` coverage still owes is over the *index*, not over any witness or drop. -/
214	theorem exists_mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T)
215	    (t : T.left) (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
216	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L]
217	    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L]
218	    [Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L]
219	    [Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L]
220	    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
221	    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L
222	        (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t) (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam))
223	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
224	    -- The `classDeg L` of `hdeg` is applied to a `relCurve`-spelled class, and the
225	    -- `BaseChangeInstances` pack is keyed to the PRODUCT spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`,
226	    -- so these three do not synthesise in the STATEMENT (a `haveI` in the proof is too late).
227	    -- They are not new assumptions: `instIsIntegralBaseChange`,
228	    -- `instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange` and `instQuasiCompactBaseChange` discharge

8	/-!
9	# B-5 assembly: from the fibre step to `chartLocus` membership over a GENERAL test
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageFibre.lean` runs `w4-datb` §1.2 steps 4–6 at a splitting field and
12	produces `IsSplitWitness` of a twisted class over `overSpec k L`.  The coverage theorem
13	(§1.2's `pic0_chartLocus_cover`) is a statement about a point `t` of a **general test** `T`:
14	
15	```
16	∃ c : ChartIndex C, t ∈ chartLocus c lam
17	```
18	
19	This file closes the gap between the two, which is one substitution and one collapse:
20	
21	* the fibre class at `t` is `picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam`, a class over the field
22	  `κ(t)` — so the fibre step applies at `K := κ(t)` with no change;
23	* `chartLocus` is *defined* as the split-witness predicate of the twisted class at that field
24	  point, and the twist commutes with restriction (`picEtMap_chartTwist`), so
25	  "`IsSplitWitness` of the twisted fibre class" **is** membership, by `Iff.rfl`.
26	
27	The second point is worth stating as a lemma rather than inlining: `chartTwist` is applied to
28	`lam` over `T` and then restricted, whereas the fibre step produces the twist of the
29	*restricted* class over `κ(t)`.  Those are equal, but not syntactically — `picEtMap_chartTwist`
30	is the law, and `mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre` is the resulting membership rule.
31	
32	## What remains of B-5 after this file
33	
34	**Twice corrected; read the DEFECT section for the full history.**  This header first said the
35	only residues were the two per-fibre choices; a degree probe added a third (step 6's feedback);
36	and on 2026-07-28 that third was **removed again** — not by discharging it but by showing
37	coverage needs no drop, hence no feedback (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`).  Step 2 is
38	likewise landed now (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean`).
39	
40	The two per-fibre choices, which are residues *of the route through this file*:
41	
42	* **step 3, the twist exponent `m`.**  Chosen against the fibre's OWN DAT-0a bound `b_L`.  No
43	  uniform `m₀` exists (§0.2.2, I-0204), so this is a genuine `∃ m` produced inside the
44	  coverage proof, at the fibre.
45	* **step 5's oracle instantiation.**  `Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`'s density keystone at
46	  `P :=` the base-changed `K_s`-points, whose `residueDeg = 1` comes from
47	  `rationalPointBaseChange_snd`.
48	
49	Both are `L`-level statements; neither is `divRep`- or certificate-gated.  Everything between
50	them and `chartLocus` membership is now landed.
51	
52	## Main declarations
53	
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre` — the membership rule: a split
55	  witness for the twisted *fibre* class puts `t` in `chartLocus`.
56	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_drop` — **the B-5 assembly**: the fibre step's
57	  hypotheses, at `K := κ(t)`, give `t ∈ chartLocus`.
58	-/

106	/-! ## A DEFECT IN THIS FILE'S OWN COMPOSITION CLAIM — read before using `mem_chartLocus_of_drop`
107	
108	Found by a degree probe on this file, the same session it was written, and stated here rather
109	than quietly repaired because the theorems below are **true and correctly proved** — what was
110	wrong is the account of how they compose.
111	
112	**The arithmetic.** `hW₀` puts `W₀` in the class `M₀ · (twist class at Z)`.  For a degree-zero
113	`λ` the presenting class `M₀` has `classDeg = 0`, so
114	
115	  `deg W₀ = m·d₁ − deg_k Z`,
116	
117	and `hdeg` demands `deg W₀ = g + e`.  Under the chart-index constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − g`
118	those force **`e = 0`**: the drop budget is zero and the greedy drop does nothing.  (Verified by
119	deriving `(e : ℤ) = 0` from exactly this hypothesis pack.)
120	
121	**What that means.** The pack is *satisfiable* — it instantiates, and at `e = 0` the theorem is
122	the true statement "a witness of degree `g` gives `chartLocus` membership".  It is not vacuous.
123	But `w4-datb` §1.2's argument runs the drop at a **different stage** from the chart index:
124	
125	* the drop runs on `λ·θᵐ` — i.e. at `Z := 0`, where `chartTwistClass C m 0 = θᵐ` and the degree
126	  is `m·d₁`, so the budget is `e = m·d₁ − g`, nonzero for the `m` step 3 chooses;
127	* its **output** `Σ` is then the chart index's `Z`, at which the twisted class has degree `g`.
128	
129	So one `Z` is an input and the other is an output, and this file's headline claim that "steps
130	4–6 are discharged" conflated them.  Steps 4 and 5 (the vanishing witness and the drop) are
131	discharged **at `Z := 0`** by `exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop`; step 6 — feeding `Σ` back as the
132	index and re-reading membership at the *new* `Z` — is **NOT** discharged, and needs the
133	graph-class transport of `Picard/Pic0ChartRationalGraph.lean` applied to the drop's output.
134	
135	**Corrected status of B-5, 2026-07-28 — and the correction is a REMOVAL of both residues this
136	section named.**  The arithmetic above is right and the two-stage reading of `w4-datb` §1.2 is
137	right; what was wrong is treating the drop as *necessary*.
138	
139	* the step-6 feedback is not a residue: coverage needs no drop at all, because
140	  `IsSplitWitness` asks for `h¹ = 0` alone (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`).  With the
141	  drop gone there is one `Z` and nothing to feed back;
142	* step 2 is landed (`PicEtAff.degAff_map` → `classDeg_presenting_eq_zero`).
143	
144	What remains of B-5 is step 3's per-fibre `m`.
145	
146	**RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (I-0660).**  This said "and even that is now *derived* rather than chosen:
147	`mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` takes the DAT-0a threshold `b_L` in the shape
148	`exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1` produces it, so instantiating DAT-0a at
149	the base-changed curve is the whole remaining work."  FALSE.  At a chart index legal at parameter
150	`n` that theorem's `hdeg` **forces** the threshold to equal `n` (`ledger_forces_b_eq_n`), and at
151	`n = g` the resulting hypothesis says every degree-`g` divisor has `h⁰ = 1`
152	(`hb_forces_h0_eq_one`) — false on a curve with a moving degree-`g` family, and strictly above
153	DAT-0a's own bound `n₁·deg F + g`.  See `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean`; the residue is
154	reconciling the chart parameter with the threshold, not instantiating DAT-0a.
155	
156	`mem_chartLocus_of_drop` stays sound and is still the right theorem when the `h⁰ = 1`
157	normalisation is wanted (DAT-C / GAP-2 need it; membership does not); use it knowing its `Z` is
158	the drop's input stage. -/

162	variable (C) in
163	/-- **THE B-5 ASSEMBLY** (`w4-datb` §1.2, everything except the two per-fibre choices).
164	
165	For a point `t` of a general test `T` and a plus class `lam` over `T`: given a finite separable
166	`L/κ(t)` presenting the fibre class, and a divisor `W₀` in the twisted class over `L` of degree
167	`g + e` with vanishing `H¹`, the point `t` lies in `chartLocus C m Z lam` — and the drop at `L`

169	
170	**Reading this against `w4-datb` §1.2 — corrected, and the earlier version of this paragraph
171	was wrong in two places** (issues I-0614, I-0615).  It said "steps 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 are all

173	
174	* **step 1 — discharged.**  The `hM₀` hypothesis, which `exists_splitting_of_picEt` supplies
175	  unconditionally.
176	* **step 2 — DISCHARGED 2026-07-28, this line supersedes the "NOT discharged" it replaced.**

182	* **step 4 — discharged** as an input: `hdeg` + `h1`.
183	* **step 5 — discharged** by the oracle.
184	* **step 6 — NOT NEEDED, which supersedes "NOT discharged".**  The feedback is real for the

195	**Note one conclusion this theorem deliberately drops** — wanted not by coverage (which needs no

197	the fibre step returns `S`'s support clause (`coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P`), and the `-` pattern below
198	discards it.  A lane closing step 6 should re-expose it — it is what says `Σ` is supported in

201	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
202	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L]
203	    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L]
204	    [Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L] [Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L]
205	    (g e : ℕ) (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
206	    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
207	    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L
208	        (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t) (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam))
209	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
210	    (W₀ : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
211	    (hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀
212	      = M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
213	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (g : ℤ) + e)
214	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1))
215	    (P : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
216	    (hdense : ∀ U : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).Opens,
217	      (U : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
218	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
219	    (hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1) :
220	    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam
221	      ∧ ∃ S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧
222	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (e : ℤ) ∧
223	        Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (W₀ - S)) = 1 ∧
224	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
225	          ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (W₀ - S)) 1) := by
226	  obtain ⟨hsplit, S, hS0, hSdeg, -, hSh0, hSh1⟩ :=
227	    exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam) m Z g e hχ M₀ hM₀
228	      W₀ hW₀ hdeg h1 P hdense hPcl hPdeg
229	  exact ⟨mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre C m Z lam t hsplit,

161	/-- **Quasi-compactness descends from a finite family of quasi-compact charts**: the base
162	`Spec k` is affine, so quasi-compactness of the structure morphism is compactness of the space
163	of the glued object, and that space is the union of the finitely many compact chart images. -/
164	theorem quasiCompact_gluedHom [Finite ι] (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
165	    QuasiCompact (gluedHom C f hf) := by
166	  haveI : Finite (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.I₀ := ‹Finite ι›

169	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace
170	  exact HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›

172	/-! ## The producer -/
173	
174	/-- **The first producer of the Jacobian datum**: a Zariski chart family of relatively
175	representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf of the degree-zero Picard functor,
176	jointly locally surjective, indexed by a finite type, with quasi-compact charts that are locally
177	of finite type over the base field, produces the pinned representability datum of the curve.
178	
179	The representing object is the glued scheme of the family, placed over `Spec k` by the
180	Σ-component of the universal element; the two certificates are `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom`
181	and `quasiCompact_gluedHom`. -/
182	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofCharts [Finite ι]
183	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
184	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
185	    JacobianData C :=
186	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
187	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
188	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
189	    (quasiCompact_gluedHom C f hf hcpt)
190	
191	@[simp]
192	lemma JacobianData.ofCharts_J [Finite ι]
193	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
194	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
195	    (JacobianData.ofCharts C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
196	  rfl
197	
198	/-- **The producer for an infinite atlas**: same as `JacobianData.ofCharts`, but the index type

200	derived from finitely many compact charts.

203	are indexed by divisor *classes* — one chart per class whose twisted fibre class has an effective

207	locally-of-finite-type certificate still descends from the charts with no finiteness hypothesis
208	whatsoever: `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` never uses `Finite ι`. -/

221	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
222	    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=

227	/-! ## The hypothesis bundle of the frozen `Jacobian` suffices
228	
229	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` introduces `[GeometricallyReduced C.hom]` before its sheaf and
230	representability statements, while the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` carries only
231	`IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  There is no gap:
232	geometric reducedness is *derived* from smoothness of relative dimension one by the global
233	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, which is in the import closure of
234	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`.  Hence every declaration above elaborates under the frozen bundle alone,
235	and the example below records it. -/
236	
237	example : GeometricallyReduced C.hom := inferInstance
238	
239	/-! ## What remains
240	
241	`JacobianData.ofCharts` reduces the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` — that is, the
242	production of `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, from which `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J` —
243	to a single geometric statement about the degree-zero Picard sheaf of the curve, namely the
244	existence of a finite Zariski atlas:
245	
246	> there exist a finite index type `ι`, schemes `X : ι → Scheme`, and morphisms of presheaves
247	> `f i : yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` such that
248	>
249	> 1. **(relative representability)** each `f i` is a relatively representable open immersion,
250	>    `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`;
251	> 2. **(coverage)** the family is jointly locally surjective for the big Zariski topology,
252	>    `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)`;
253	> 3. **(chart finiteness)** each chart is locally of finite type over the base field with
254	>    respect to its own structure morphism, `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`, and each
255	>    chart space is quasi-compact, `CompactSpace (X i)`.
256	
257	Nothing else about the Picard functor is needed: the sheaf condition is already discharged
258	(`pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf`), the gluing is mathlib's (`Scheme.LocalRepresentability`), the
259	Σ-descent to the slice is already discharged (`Functor.RepresentableBy.overSlice`), and the two
260	certificates of the glued object are discharged here from (3).
261	
262	Conditions (1) and (2) are the geometric input — they are what the divisor-scheme/Abel-map
263	machinery of the `DivScheme…` and `DivRep…` files exists to produce, one chart being carved out
264	of a symmetric power of the curve by an effectivity locus.  Condition (3) is a property of those
265	charts alone and does not interact with the Picard functor at all.
266	
267	If the atlas that machinery produces is *not* finitely indexed — and the classical one is not,
268	its charts being indexed by divisor classes — then `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace` is the
269	form to use: `ι` is then arbitrary, condition (3) weakens to `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`
270	alone, and the second certificate becomes the single statement `CompactSpace` of the glued
271	object.  That statement is not a bookkeeping hypothesis but a theorem about the Jacobian — the
272	underlying space is the image of a quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map — and it is
273	where the quasi-compactness content of the construction actually lives. -/
274	
275	end AlgebraicGeometry

38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/
41	
42	set_option autoImplicit false
43	
44	universe u
45	
46	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
47	
48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
49	
50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
51	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
52	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
53	
54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl
70	
71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem
143	
144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩
150	
151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
152	
153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice
170	
171	end AlgebraicGeometry

10	
11	`Picard/JacobianDataAbelImage.lean` reduced DAT-J's quasi-compactness field to a single
12	statement, `Function.Surjective abel.base` — *step 3* of `informal/w4-datj-worksheet.md`

14	Picard theory supplies: *every field point of `J.left` is a degree-zero class over its
15	residue field, shift it by `fiberTwist`, take an effective representative, and that
16	representative is a `DivScheme`-point hitting the original point.*
17	
18	That argument produces, for a point `y`, a **morphism** `Spec κ(y) ⟶ DivScheme g` — not an
19	element of the fibre of `abel.base` over `y`.  Nothing in the tree converted the first into
20	the second, and it is not bookkeeping that can be skipped: the target of DJ-1 is a statement
21	about the underlying *topological* map, while everything the Picard side produces is a
22	morphism of schemes.
23	
24	This file supplies exactly that conversion, and nothing else:
25	
26	> `surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` — if for every `y : Y` some
27	> `q : Spec (Y.residueField y) ⟶ X` satisfies `q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y`, then
28	> `f.base` is surjective.
29	
30	The proof is `Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField` (mathlib): the range of
31	`Y.fromSpecResidueField y` is `{y}`, and `Spec κ(y)` is nonempty because `κ(y)` is a field,
32	so any point of `Spec κ(y)` maps into the fibre.  Composed with the DJ-0 lemmas this gives
33	the Jacobian datum producers in the shape the classical argument actually delivers: a
34	*per-point lift*, which is what `exists_effective_of_picClass` hands back.
35

37	
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` — the conversion.
39	  Pure scheme topology; no curve, no Picard functor, no divisor scheme.
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_forall_residueField_lift_from_divScheme` — DJ-1's qc
41	  step from per-point lifts.
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` and
43	  `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelLifts` — the two `JacobianData` producers
44	  with the surjectivity hypothesis replaced by per-point lifts.

48	It produces no lift.  Producing one is the divRep-gated mathematics of §2.3 (the
49	`fiberTwist` shift plus `exists_effective_of_picClass`, which must stay Challenge-free per
50	§0.5 — `riemann_inequality`, never `riemann_inequality_curve`).  What changes is the shape

72	underlying map of `f` is surjective.

74	`Spec κ(y)` is nonempty (a field is nontrivial), and the range of `Y.fromSpecResidueField y`
75	is `{y}` (mathlib `Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField`), so the image under `q` of any point

91	  have hs : (q ≫ f).base s = (Y.fromSpecResidueField y).base s := by rw [hq]

8	/-!
9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
15	
16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
23	
24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
25	
26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
32	
33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
34	
35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
40	  the freedom.
41	
42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
57	  chart parameter.
58	-/

76	variable (C π) in
77	/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**
78	
79	Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
80	`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
81	*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`

87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
89	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)

93	    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
94	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)

98	family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.
99	
100	So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
101	different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
102	condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/

104	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
105	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
106	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
108	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
109	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
110	    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
111	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
112	  huniv i

115	/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**
116	
117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
118	question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
119	never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
120	carries no uniformity obligation.
121	
122	Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
123	CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
124	than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
125	def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
126	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
127	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
128	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
129	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
130	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
131	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
132	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
133	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
134	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
135	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
136	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
137	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
138	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf
139
